constraints: Cannot be used on the currently-open data file.
Can only be executed from 4D in local mode or from 4D Server (as a stored procedure); not available in remote mode.
The dataPath data file must correspond to the structurePath structure file; only tables set as 'encryptable' are affected.
This is a lengthy operation that displays a (user-interruptible) progress indicator and includes a compacting step.

The original files are never modified in place; they are moved into a timestamped backup folder ('Replaced files (Encrypting|Decrypting) YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS'), inside archiveFolder if provided, or next to the structure file otherwise; the command's return value is the path to that backup folder.
A new*/current* passphrase or data key not supplied to the command can instead be supplied via the 4D keychain; the newPassPhrase/newDataKey used is itself never added to the keychain.

methodName, if valid, is called as a progress/status callback taking up to 5 parameters ($messageType, $objectType, $messageText, $table, $reserved) for message/finished/error/end-of-execution/warning events.

overloadPatches.semanticRole: Encrypts, re-encrypts, or decrypts the data file using passphrase-derived keys (SHA-256) for both the new and, if re-encrypting, current credential.

jointConstraints.rule: For first-time encryption, pass only newPassPhrase and omit curPassPhrase. For re-encrypting an already-encrypted database, pass both (curPassPhrase may instead come from the 4D keychain). To remove encryption entirely, pass an empty string as newPassPhrase while still supplying curPassPhrase.

overloadPatches.semanticRole: Encrypts, re-encrypts, or decrypts the data file using explicit encryption-key objects (from New data key) for both the new and, if re-encrypting, current credential.

jointConstraints.rule: For first-time encryption, pass only newDataKey and omit curDataKey. For re-encrypting an already-encrypted database, pass both (curDataKey may instead come from the 4D keychain). To remove encryption entirely, pass a null data key as newDataKey while still supplying curDataKey.

overloadPatches.semanticRole: Re-encrypts a database that is currently keyed by an explicit data-key object, switching it to a new passphrase-derived key.

jointConstraints.rule: This mixed form re-encrypts a database whose current key is an explicit data-key object (curDataKey), replacing it with a passphrase-derived key (newPassPhrase); both must be supplied together (curDataKey may instead come from the 4D keychain).
